name: Staged, rugless: the LISABO 78 3/4 ash across the room, parallel to the living room, four LISABO chairs, the pendant over it, the buffet and art on the bottom wall
notes:
Staged 2026-10-26 (evening) on Andrew's word ("flip it. remove the random kids chair, shes almost 5, can sit on a regular chair." and "remove the circle table layouts I hate cirlce tabnles."): the LISABO 78 3/4" ash turned across the room, parallel to the living room, x 30-108.75, y 62.25-93: its kitchen end on that walkway's edge (F-42), 19 1/4" of dead floor at the right wall (no seat fits there), 32.25" from its living-room side to that walkway's edge (the chairs there sit with their backs to the living room, 11" inside the clearance, and push back into the walkway by about 9" when someone stands up) and 26" from its other side to the bottom wall (tight:26, F-36; those chairs push back under the floating buffet, 33" up, and nobody passes behind them). Four LISABO ash/Tallmyra chairs, two a side; Maddie, almost 5, sits on a regular chair (no junior chair); six seats fit along the sides when more chairs come.
Against j (the table along the room's depth, staged until he said flip it): 32 and 26" on the chair sides instead of 33.6" on both; the long side toward the living room, so the table reads wide from the sofa, instead of toward the kitchen; the cook steps from the kitchen to the table's end instead of its side; and the table runs across the oak floor's grain toward the kitchen's tile line instead of parallel to it. Both work; j keeps both walkways cleaner, this one reads wider from the sofa and he chose it.
The rest: the pendant over the table's center, the buffet drawn but not ordered, the art and lamps, the plant; no rug (F-66).
Total $1,443.88: placed $1,384.94 + extras $58.94; prices as of 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-26 (those before today price-stale, F-02).
Flags across the layout: tight:26 (the wall side, F-36). The round ROSENTORP layout (c) is gone: Andrew hates circle tables.
